expectedText:
PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACTOR REGISTRATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACTOR REGISTRATION INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's public-works contractor registration requirement, Labor Code Section 1725.5, and the related bid-and-award rules of Labor Code Section 1771.1, which govern who must register with the Department of Industrial Relations before bidding on, being listed as a subcontractor in a bid proposal for, or performing work on a contract for public work, as well as the parallel registration track created by Labor Code Section 1725.6 for certain non-public-works development projects that are nonetheless subject to prevailing wage and skilled-workforce requirements. Acme, Inc. has described its involvement in public works contracting, if any, as follows: We bid on and perform road construction contracts for local municipalities. This document states the content of the statutes; it does not determine whether Acme, Inc. or any particular project or contract falls within the statutory scope of "public work" or of the referenced Government Code development streamlining provisions, and it is not a substitute for individualized legal advice or for consulting a licensed attorney.

REGISTRATION REQUIRED TO BID, BE LISTED, OR PERFORM ON PUBLIC WORK
Labor Code Section 1725.5 states that a contractor must be registered under that section to be qualified to bid on, be listed in a bid proposal for, or engage in the performance of any public work contract subject to the prevailing wage chapter, and that for this purpose "contractor" includes a subcontractor as defined in Labor Code Section 1722.1.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A contractor shall be registered pursuant to this section to be qualified to bid on, be listed in a bid proposal, subject to the requirements of Section 4104 of the Public Contract Code, or engage in the performance of any public work contract that is subject to the requirements of this chapter."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, registration required to bid on, be listed in a bid proposal for, or perform public work (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The quoted sentence does not itself define "public work" or state the scope of "this chapter"; those definitions and scope limits appear in other sections of the same prevailing wage chapter (beginning at Labor Code Section 1720) that are outside this citation and are not reproduced here, so this sheet does not by itself establish whether a given contract is a "public work" in the first place.

WHAT A CONTRACTOR MUST SHOW TO QUALIFY FOR REGISTRATION
Labor Code Section 1725.5(a) states that, in addition to registering and paying the application and renewal fees, a contractor must provide evidence, disclosures, or releases establishing several things, among them that the contractor carries workers' compensation coverage sufficient for any worker performing prevailing-wage work, that the contractor is appropriately licensed under the Business and Professions Code where applicable, that the contractor has no delinquent liability to an employee or the state for back wages or related damages under a final judgment or administrative determination (subject to an appeal-bond exception), and that the contractor is not currently debarred under Labor Code Section 1777.1 or other federal or state debarment law.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Workers’ compensation coverage that meets the requirements of Division 4 (commencing with Section 3200) and includes sufficient coverage for any worker whom the contractor employs to perform work that is subject to prevailing wage requirements other than a contractor who is separately registered under this section."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(a)(2)(A) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, workers' compensation coverage requirement for registration (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  "The contractor is not currently debarred under Section 1777.1 or under any other federal or state law providing for the debarment of contractors from public works."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(a)(2)(D) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, no-current-debarment requirement for registration (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The statute lists what a contractor must show but does not itself describe the registration portal, application form, or documentation format the Department of Industrial Relations requires to make that showing; those mechanics are set by department procedure rather than by the quoted statutory text, so this sheet does not describe the actual registration process.

TWELVE-MONTH LOOKBACK FOR PRIOR UNREGISTERED BIDDING OR WORK, AND THE REGISTRATION-FEE CURE
Labor Code Section 1725.5(a)(2)(E) states that, to qualify for registration, a contractor must not have bid on a public works contract, been listed in a bid proposal, or performed public works without being lawfully registered within the preceding 12 months (or since the requirement first applied, whichever is earlier). The same paragraph states that this disqualification is waived if the contractor has not previously been found in violation within the preceding 12 months and pays an additional nonrefundable penalty registration fee of $2,000.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The contractor has not bid on a public works contract, been listed in a bid proposal, or engaged in the performance of a contract for public works without being lawfully registered in accordance with this section, within the preceding 12 months or since the effective date of the requirements set forth in subdivision (e), whichever is earlier"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(a)(2)(E) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, 12-month lookback disqualification for prior unregistered bidding or work (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The statute states that disqualification applies if a contractor "is found to be in violation," but the quoted paragraph does not identify who makes that finding or what process applies to it; that determination appears to draw on the civil wage and penalty assessment procedures elsewhere in this chapter (see Labor Code Sections 1741-1742), which are not quoted or analyzed in this clause.

CONSEQUENCE OF AN UNPAID RENEWAL FEE, AND THE INADVERTENCE CURE
Labor Code Section 1725.5(c) states that a contractor who fails to pay the annual renewal fee by the expiration of the prior registration period is prohibited from bidding on or performing any public work contract until registered again, but that if the failure to pay was inadvertent, the contractor may renew retroactively by paying an additional nonrefundable penalty renewal fee equal to the amount of the renewal fee, within 90 days of the renewal fee's due date.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A contractor who fails to pay the renewal fee required under paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) on or before the expiration of any prior period of registration shall be prohibited from bidding on or engaging in the performance of any contract for public work until once again registered pursuant to this section."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(c) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, consequence of failing to pay the annual renewal fee (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The subdivision does not address what happens to work already in progress under a contract that was validly bid while the contractor was registered, if the registration then lapses mid-performance before the 90-day inadvertence cure is used; its interaction with the separate bid-and-contract bar in Labor Code Section 1771.1(a) for that scenario is not addressed in the quoted text.

DOLLAR-THRESHOLD EXEMPTION FOR SMALL PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS
Labor Code Section 1725.5(f) states that the registration requirement does not apply to work on a public works project of $25,000 or less for construction, alteration, demolition, installation, or repair work, or to work on a public works project of $15,000 or less for maintenance work.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "This section does not apply to work performed on a public works project of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) or less when the project is for construction, alteration, demolition, installation, or repair work or to work performed on a public works project of fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) or less when the project is for maintenance work."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(f) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, small public works project dollar-threshold exemption (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The subdivision states flat dollar thresholds without an inflation adjustment mechanism and without specifying how the threshold is measured for a project performed under multiple change orders, phased task orders, or an indefinite-quantity contract; those measurement questions are not addressed in the quoted text.

PHASE-IN DATES AND THE SECTION'S CURRENT OPERATIVE DATE
Labor Code Section 1725.5(e) states that the registration requirement applies to any bid proposal submitted on or after March 1, 2015, to any public work contract executed on or after April 1, 2015, and to any work performed under a public work contract on or after January 1, 2018, regardless of when the contract was executed. The current version of the section, which restates and renumbers the requirement, states in subdivision (h) that it became operative on July 1, 2026.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The requirements of this section shall apply to any bid proposal submitted on or after March 1, 2015, to any contract for public work, as defined in this chapter, executed on or after April 1, 2015, and to any work performed under a contract for public work on or after January 1, 2018, regardless of when the contract for public work was executed."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(e) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, original 2015/2018 phase-in dates for the registration requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  "This section shall become operative on July 1, 2026."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(h) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, current operative date of the section as amended (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The version of Section 1725.5 checked here was added by Stats. 2023, Chapter 39, Section 24, and then amended by Stats. 2024, Chapter 52, Section 22, with an operative date of July 1, 2026; the quoted text does not itself explain what registration rule (if any) governed public works bidding and performance between the 2023 enactment and the July 1, 2026 operative date of this current version, so the transitional period is not covered by this sheet.

THE PARALLEL REGISTRATION TRACK FOR CERTAIN NON-PUBLIC-WORKS DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS
Labor Code Section 1725.6 creates a second, separately numbered registration requirement for a contractor to be awarded, or to perform work on, projects or developments subject to specified Government Code streamlined-housing-approval statutes (Sections 65852.24, 65912.130, 65912.131, 65913.4, and 65913.16), or any other project where a statute or regulation requires registration under Section 1725.6, even where the project is not a "public work" governed by Section 1725.5. A contractor who has already paid the registration or renewal fee under Section 1725.6 is not required to pay a second registration or renewal fee to also register under Section 1725.5, and the reverse is likewise true.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A contractor shall be registered pursuant to this section to be qualified to be awarded contracts for, or engage in the performance of, any work on projects or developments subject to the requirements of Section 65852.24, 65912.130, 65912.131, 65913.4, or 65913.16 of the Government Code or any work on projects or developments where a statute or regulation requires registration pursuant to this section."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.6 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, registration requirement for specified streamlined-housing development projects (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.6.)
  "A contractor that has paid the registration or renewal fee and is registered under Section 1725.6 shall not pay the registration or renewal fee required under paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) to register as a contractor under this section."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1725.5(g) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, registration under Section 1725.6 satisfies the Section 1725.5 fee (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1725.5.)
  Known gap: The quoted text does not explain why the Legislature created a second, structurally near-identical registration section instead of expanding Section 1725.5's own scope, and it does not state whether the Government Code housing-streamlining provisions it cross-references define "contractor" the same way as Labor Code Section 1722.1 does for purposes of Section 1725.5; that potential definitional difference is not addressed here.

THE AWARDING BODY'S OWN NOTICE AND BID-REJECTION DUTIES
Labor Code Section 1771.1 places obligations on the body awarding a public works contract, not only on the contractor: notice of the registration requirement must be included in all bid invitations and public works contracts, and a bid may not be accepted, nor a contract or subcontract entered into, without proof of the contractor's or subcontractor's current registration under Section 1725.5. The Department of Industrial Relations is separately required to maintain a public list, on its internet website, of contractors currently registered to perform public work.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Notice of the requirement described in subdivision (a) shall be included in all bid invitations and public works contracts, and a bid shall not be accepted nor any contract or subcontract entered into without proof of the contractor or subcontractor’s current registration to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1771.1(b) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, awarding body's notice and bid-acceptance duties (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1771.1.)
  "The department shall maintain on its internet website a list of contractors who are currently registered to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1771.1(e) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, Department of Industrial Relations' public registered-contractor list (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1771.1.)
  Known gap: Subdivision (a) also states that it is not a violation for an unregistered contractor to submit certain bids authorized under specified Business and Professions Code and Public Contract Code sections, provided registration occurs by contract award; those cross-referenced exceptions are named but not reproduced or analyzed here, so this clause does not describe their full scope.

CIVIL PENALTIES FOR PERFORMING PUBLIC WORK WHILE UNREGISTERED, INCLUDING HIGHER-TIER CONTRACTOR EXPOSURE
Labor Code Section 1771.1(g) states that a contractor or subcontractor found by the Labor Commissioner to have performed public work without being registered forfeits a civil penalty of $100 for each day of work performed in violation, up to an aggregate of $8,000. Separately, subdivision (h)(1) states that a higher-tiered contractor or subcontractor found to have subcontracted with an unregistered lower-tier subcontractor to perform public work is itself subject to forfeiture of $100 per day the unregistered lower-tier subcontractor performs work, up to an aggregate of $10,000.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "the contractor or subcontractor shall forfeit, as a civil penalty to the state, one hundred dollars ($100) for each day of work performed in violation of the registration requirement, not to exceed an aggregate penalty of eight thousand dollars ($8,000)"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1771.1(g) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code, civil penalty for a contractor or subcontractor performing unregistered public work (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1771.1.)
  "a higher tiered public works contractor or subcontractor who is found to have entered into a subcontract with an unregistered lower tier subcontractor to perform any public work in violation of the requirements of Section 1725.5 or this section shall be subject to forfeiture, as a civil penalty to the state, of one hundred dollars ($100) for each day the unregistered lower tier subcontractor performs work in violation of the registration requirement, not to exceed an aggregate penalty of ten thousand dollars ($10,000)"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1771.1(h)(1) (California Legislative Information text; same section as the preceding citation, not an independent source of it), California Labor Code, civil penalty for a higher-tiered contractor engaging an unregistered lower-tier subcontractor (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=1771.1.)
  Known gap: Subdivision (h) also states, in paragraphs not quoted here, that a higher-tiered contractor is not liable under this provision if the lower-tier subcontractor's violation stems from revocation of a previously approved registration, and that a lower-tier subcontractor cannot itself be held liable for a higher-tiered contractor's penalty or be required to indemnify it; this clause states the penalty amounts but does not restate those liability-allocation carve-outs in full.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding California's public-works contractor registration requirements, Labor Code Sections 1725.5, 1725.6, and 1771.1, was prepared by Jordan T. Reyes for Acme, Inc. and reviewed in Oakland, California on September 1, 2026. It reflects the statutory text as of the date checked above and does not reflect any amendments made after that date, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney.

It reflects the statutory text as of the date checked above and does not reflect any amendments made after that date, and it is not a substitute for consulting a licensed attorney.
